india_read_through: Brent down about 1.1% falls in the +1 band (down 0.5% to 2%). It follows a 7.6% fall on Nov 2, so two straight declines ease pressure on the trade deficit, rupee and inflation, but the level above $100 is still a heavy import bill. Inflation: lower crude trims fuel and input cost risk, but little relief at these levels. Rupee: mildly supportive via a smaller oil import bill. OMCs (BPCL, HPCL, IOC): lower crude helps marketing margins. Paints, aviation (ATF) and tyres (crude-linked raw materials): mild cost relief. Upstream (ONGC, Oil India): lower realisations are a mild negative. Metals: copper down about 2.5% is a soft cue for Hindalco, Vedanta and Hindustan Copper, a small weight for the index; aluminium not available. Gold financiers (Muthoot, Manappuram): gold lower by about 0.7% and below $4,000 is a mild negative for loan-book collateral value and sentiment, though the effect is small.
risks: Iran-US talks are unresolved and a US strike report on Qeshm Island was cited; headline reversals could send crude sharply higher.
Crude is volatile (7.6% fall on Nov 2, then 1.1% fall) and still above $100.
